static_traits.name: Madeline
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationship with archery friends due to own lack of enthusiasm and progress, not yet sharing frustration with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem history; not yet received psychotherapy or counseling; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Rather negative tone, hesitant but willing to try; can describe experiences and timeline concretely; tending to compare with others and negate positive evidence; clear expression, average cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: Recently started archery lessons and enjoying them, but I always feel I have not improved, which makes me consider quitting.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realized my negative thoughts about my archery progress are affecting my motivation to continue the sport.

special_situations.event: Seeing other students' scores and skills constantly improving in archery class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my progress is not as good as others', it means I have failed and have no ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces communication with friends, avoids sharing frustration; sets small goals to try to motivate themselves but still considers giving up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as they are, I am terrible, I should quit

special_situations.event: Repeatedly not yet able to steadily hit the bullseye in practice
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot consistently hit the target, it proves I am completely unskilled at archery
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using 'simply not practicing anymore' to avoid failing again; attributing rare successes to 'luck' instead of acknowledging their value
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible at archery, nothing I do will make it better

special_situations.event: When reviewing training progress, only focuses on my own mistakes, ignoring the number of hits and improvements
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only perfect performance counts as progress, sporadic successes do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, interpreting success as 'just luck'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those hits are not real progress, I am still a failure

special_situations.event: Full-time work leaves limited practice time; feels hard to balance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot invest much time practicing, no progress is possible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing practice frequency, decreased motivation, considering stopping the course
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not have enough time to practice, so I definitely will not improve

core_conflict.wish: Longing to have her progress and ability seen and recognized (performing well in archery)
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure and lagging in comparison, worried about exposing incompetence and being judged by others
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged by keeping distance and not sharing feelings
Maintaining a consistent 'failure' self-schema by negating positive feedback, to avoid uncertainty
Avoids further frustration by considering giving up

object_relations.self_representation: A stagnant learner / failure, not good enough
object_relations.object_representation: Classmates and friends are more excellent others who will judge oneself

object_relations.self_representation: Someone who should not trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Friends are people who may be dragged down by her and will not understand her

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to identify and accept positive evidence in practice (like increased hits) or suggests recording successful experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing the counselor's encouragement as 'demanding she prove herself', believing these successes are just luck and cannot show she is truly capable
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'insufficient evidence' and 'just luck' in a calm but skeptical tone, listing counterexamples to negate positive observations, avoiding emotional display.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they are willing to share feelings of frustration with friends or others and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing sharing will trouble others, meeting misunderstanding or implicit judgment (transference: seeing others as rejecters)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing 'do not want to trouble others' in self-reproaching language, politely declining sharing and help, restrained tone, ending the topic quickly.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out she already shows signs of progress (such as hitting more times than in the past)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feeling these improvements are not real or sustainable, worried she will still fail
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Directly negating with words like 'this does not count' / 'just coincidence', keeping answers brief and returning to the negative narrative.

manifestations: When seeing no sustained progress, feeling practice loses meaning and joy
Treats sporadic successes as 'luck', difficult to give them meaning
Unwilling to share frustration with classmates, believing they will not understand
Reduced interpersonal interaction,Tense relationships with friends
outcomes: Reduced social support, further weakening motivation to persist

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self; that is, the individual redirects the energy originally meant to be sent outward back toward the self, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language expressions include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it' and 'I should not trouble others'.
manifestations: Not sharing frustration with friends, worried about troubling others
Digests stress and disappointment inwardly, reducing outward support-seeking

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on.
manifestations: Believing friends will not understand her and will judge her
In comparisons, binds others' progress with their own failure, feeling influenced by others' gazes

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on.
manifestations: Excessive self-blame; focuses only on mistakes and flaws
Negating progress, viewing positive evidence cautiously, hard to accept positive experiences

exception_events.target_problem: When missing shots or comparing with classmates in archery class, the client usually engages in self-denial, developing thoughts of quitting and reduced practice motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In some practice sessions, she hit the target more times than before, and noticed it was easier to hit than when she started; at the time she did not immediately engage in self-denial as usual.
exception_events.reason: Clues: had previously tried setting small goals and practicing consistently; objective feedback (increased number of hits) provided them with evidence of progress.

positive_force: Interested in archery, willing to invest and try new methods (such as setting small goals, accepting counseling, and doing homework)
Segments of objective progress already exist (number of hits increased)
Has potential peer support resources (has archery friends)
Able to express problems and emotions clearly; willing to explore new perspectives
negative_force: Prominent cognitive distortions like comparison and despair, black-and-white thinking, and mental filtering
Tending to negate positive feedback, with harsh self-evaluation
Unwilling to ask others for help, worried about troubling them, leaving the support system not yet used
Conflict between work and practice time intensifies helplessness and anticipated failure

target_behavior.behavior: Strong frustration and self-denial during archery practice, developing thoughts of quitting
antecedent: Not yet able to hit the target during practice
Entering a plateau about a month after starting the course
Practice time limited by full-time work
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative core beliefs about ability and cognitive distortions (mental filtering, black-and-white thinking, comparison) reinforcing failure experiences
target_behavior.function: Escaping failure and shame, temporarily relieving anxiety and pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased practice drive, avoiding practice; interest and motivation for other activities affected; relationship tension with archery friends

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding sharing frustration and seeking peer support
antecedent: Thinking about talking to peers or friends about one's difficulties
Feeling she would trouble others or be misunderstood
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of being judged and rejected, using defenses like retroflection and projection to maintain a sense of safety
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluations and interpersonal discomfort
target_behavior.consequence: Support system not yet used, interpersonal relationships distanced, increased loneliness
